pcp.claim-10.markdown: Lee's implementation finds the field, generators and cube roots by bounded search in time polynomial in $q$, hence in the input length, and compiles the verifier into Mathlib's finite multi-stack machine model with a polynomial cost bound.

pcp.claim-reference-np-equivalence.markdown: explicit simulations identify its witness class with [the NP class in the unchanged vendored ComplexityLib][lean-reference-np].

pcp.claim-source-11.markdown: For completeness, a proper colouring, its low-degree extension, exact vanishing certificates and honest lines tables, with degrees below $b^c$, pass every check for every seed: one fixed eight-table proof with perfect completeness.

pcp.claim-source-12.markdown: After fair-bit sampling the rejection gap is at least $g_c/16$, and constantly many independent repetitions on the same proof reduce soundness error to $1/2$, keeping logarithmic randomness and constant queries.

pcp.claim-source-13.markdown: For the converse, take the verifier and bounds $p,\alpha,\beta$ of Theorem 1.1, guess the first $p(n)$ proof bits and simulate the verifier, in polynomial time, on each of the at most $2^\beta(2(n+2))^\alpha$ random strings. Perfect completeness gives a prefix accepted on every run. If such a prefix existed for a no-instance, its zero extension would have acceptance probability one, contradicting soundness. The resulting witness relation is decidable in polynomial time, so the language lies in NP.
